lines: ZERO just got his first credit card.
This is its first coffee.
That café has never met ZERO.
His bank has never met the café.
So who decides to trust him?
Between this tap and that cup, a tiny message will cross three companies,
survive a fraud test,
and come back with a yes or a no.
ZERO is riding it.
First surprise:
that card has no battery.
The terminal's radio field wakes up its chip for a split second,
just long enough to say one thing.
To ZERO, it's his money.
To the system, it's this.
A card number.
An amount.
Which shop.
And a code that only works once.
Copy that code,
and it's useless a second later.
That's why a chip card is so hard to clone.
Pay with a phone instead,
and even the card number is fake.
It's a stand-in called a token.
Visa says it has handed out more than sixteen billion of them.
ZERO thinks it's going straight to his bank.
It isn't.
Not even close.
